Returns a texture that shows one rectangle of a texture atlas made with [LoadAtlas](LoadAtlas). The rectangle is given in pixels. The new texture has no picture of its own: it uses the image of the atlas, and only remembers which part of it to show, so it costs next to nothing. The result is used like any other texture, with [EntityTexture](EntityTexture), [BrushTexture](BrushTexture) and so on. [TextureWidth](TextureWidth) and [TextureHeight](TextureHeight) tell the size of the rectangle.

Each tile has its own [ScaleTexture](ScaleTexture), [PositionTexture](PositionTexture), [RotateTexture](RotateTexture), [TextureBlend](TextureBlend) and [TextureCoords](TextureCoords) settings, which work inside the rectangle (like frames of [LoadAnimTexture](LoadAnimTexture), the coordinates do not repeat inside the tile, so values beyond 0 to 1 show the neighbouring tiles). The flags are the ones of the atlas; mip maps are only used if the atlas was loaded with a gutter.

Without a gutter (see [LoadAtlas](LoadAtlas)) the tile uses the first mip level only, and to keep the neighbouring tile out of linear filtering, the rectangle is shrunk by half a texel on every side. A tile therefore looks very slightly zoomed in, and nothing of what is next to it can shine through. With the point flag (1024) the tile is exact.

[FreeTexture](FreeTexture) on a tile only frees the tile. [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer) and [SaveTexture](SaveTexture) are not available for tiles: use the atlas.
@param atlas   A texture made by LoadAtlas.
@param x       Left edge of the rectangle in pixels.
@param y       Top edge of the rectangle in pixels.
@param width   Width of the rectangle in pixels.
@param height  Height of the rectangle in pixels.
@returns A texture handle, or 0 if the rectangle is not completely inside the atlas.
